prose.text:
Superconductivity
In $1911$, the Dutch physicist Kamerlingh Onnes discovered superconductivity.

Resistance describes how strongly a conductor opposes electric current under specified conditions.
Current is the amount of electric charge flowing past a place per unit time.

He cooled mercury in liquid helium.
At first its resistance changed gradually;
then the source describes it suddenly dropping to zero at $4.1\mathrm{K}$, as in Figure 172.

K labels kelvin, a unit of temperature;
smaller kelvin values mean lower temperatures.

Later, many other pure metals and alloys were found to become superconducting at very low temperatures.
An alloy combines a metal with other elements.
Different materials have different conditions for entering this state.

Superconductivity involves more than zero electrical resistance.
It also has the Meissner effect: under suitable weak-magnetic-field conditions, the material excludes magnetic field from its interior.
A magnetic field describes magnetic effects at each place, so an ideal perfect conductor with zero resistance is not automatically a superconductor.
prose.source_text: $1911$年荷兰物理学家卡曼林·盎曼斯发现了著名的现象——超导电性. 他发现当水银在液态氦中冷却时，它的电阻开始逐渐地变化，而后，当温度为$4.1\mathrm{K}$时，电阻突然降到零(图172). 后来，又发现有很多纯金属和合金，在很低的温度时变为超导状态.

p0222#10 names the historical discoverer of superconductivity; retain the exact source transliteration.

prose.text:
The source discusses low-temperature superconductivity observed below $20\mathrm{K}$ and lists transition temperatures for some materials in an appendix.
A transition temperature marks a change into the superconducting state under specified conditions.
The book's stated temperature range is not a common upper limit for every superconducting material.

Other materials can become superconducting at higher temperatures.
Each material has its own transition conditions.
Being cold alone does not guarantee that a material is superconducting.
prose.source_text: 在很低的温度：$20\mathrm{K}$以下，可以观察到超导电性现象. 在书末的附表中列出了一些物质转变为超导状态的温度.

prose.text:
A persistent current
The source describes first establishing current in a closed ring of superconducting conductor and then removing the electrical supply.
A closed ring provides an unbroken path for the current.

In the ideal case where the superconducting state is maintained, with no disturbance or energy dissipation, the current remains unchanged.
This is called a persistent current.
Dissipation means useful energy being converted into other forms, such as heat.

A real superconducting ring must remain within suitable temperature, magnetic-field, and current limits.
Persistent does not mean unchanged under every possible condition.
In an ordinary resistive, nonsuperconducting ring, the current decreases and soon disappears after the supply is removed.
prose.source_text: 如果在处于超导状态的环形导体中形成电流，然后撤掉电源，则电流强度永不改变. 在一般非超导体中，这种情况下的电流很快地消失.

prose.text:
Applications and limits
Superconductors have practical uses, including coils in powerful electromagnets.

An electromagnet uses electric current to produce a magnetic field.
In a closed coil that remains superconducting, steady current causes no electrical-resistance heating.

The coil can maintain a magnetic field for a long time without continually replacing that part of the electrical energy loss.
This does not mean that the whole electromagnet uses no energy.
Establishing its current and field takes energy, and cooling equipment also needs energy.
prose.source_text: 超导体具有广泛的实际应用. 例如，制造具有超导线圈的大功率电磁铁，这种超导线圈产生磁场，在很长的时间里不消耗能量. 因为在超导线圈中不放出热量.

prose.text:
The magnetic field a superconducting magnet can produce is limited by its material.
The source's warning about strong magnetic fields means fields beyond the allowed critical conditions can destroy the superconducting state.
It does not mean that every superconducting magnet is unable to produce a strong field.

A changing magnetic field can induce current in a superconductor.
Induce means cause current through the effect of a changing magnetic field.
The conductor's current also produces its own magnetic field.

Each superconducting conductor therefore has a critical current, a limit beyond which its superconducting state cannot be guaranteed.
The critical magnetic field and critical current depend on the material, temperature, and magnetic-field conditions.
All these limits must be considered when using a coil.
prose.source_text: 然而，利用超导磁体不能产生强磁场. 强磁场要破坏超导状态. 强磁场可以在超导体本身中产生电流. 因此，对于处在超导状态的每一个导体来说，都有一个电流的临界值，电流强度达到临界值时，超导状态不被破坏是不可能的.

prose.text:
The source also reports that superconductors were used as small memory devices in computers of its time.
A memory device stores information.
This is a historical use described by the book, not a statement that today's computers generally use such devices.
prose.source_text: 超导体用于近代计算机中，作为小型的记忆装置.

prose.text:
A possibility for transmitting energy
The book imagines superconducting materials that work near room temperature and are suitable for practical electrical transmission.

In an ideal steady direct-current system that maintains superconductivity without disturbances or dissipation, these wires could avoid direct-current resistance losses.
Direct current maintains a fixed direction in this steady model.

The material would still have to satisfy magnetic-field and current limits.
Alternating current, which changes direction over time, or changing magnetic fields can still produce losses in superconducting wire itself.
Avoiding this particular wire loss does not make an entire transmission system free of every energy loss.

Finding suitable superconducting materials is an important technical aim of physics research.
prose.source_text: 假如在接近室温的温度下有超导材料，则可以解决重要的技术问题：能量沿着导线传递没有损失. 当然物理学的工作就是要解决这个问题.

prose.text:
Explaining superconductivity requires quantum mechanics, the theory used to describe matter at the microscopic level.
The source states that a microscopic explanation of conventional superconductivity was given in $1957$.
This does not mean that superconductivity in every material had been explained that year.
prose.source_text: 只有根据量子力学，才能解释超导电性. 在$1957$年才给出了解释.

data.chapter: 第二编 电动力学基础
data.title: 超导电性

prose.text: $1911$年荷兰物理学家卡曼林·盎曼斯发现了著名的现象——超导电性. 他发现当水银在液态氦中冷却时，它的电阻开始逐渐地变化，而后，当温度为$4.1\mathrm{K}$时，电阻突然降到零(图172). 后来，又发现有很多纯金属和合金，在很低的温度时变为超导状态.
在很低的温度：$20\mathrm{K}$以下，可以观察到超导电性现象. 在书末的附表中列出了一些物质转变为超导状态的温度.
如果在处于超导状态的环形导体中形成电流，然后撤掉电源，则电流强度永不改变. 在一般非超导体中，这种情况下的电流很快地消失.
超导体具有广泛的实际应用. 例如，制造具有超导线圈的大功率电磁铁，这种超导线圈产生磁场，在很长的时间里不消耗能量. 因为在超导线圈中不放出热量.
然而，利用超导磁体不能产生强磁场. 强磁场要破坏超导状态. 强磁场可以在超导体本身中产生电流. 因此，对于处在超导状态的每一个导体来说，都有一个电流的临界值，电流强度达到临界值时，超导状态不被破坏是不可能的.
超导体用于近代计算机中，作为小型的记忆装置.
假如在接近室温的温度下有超导材料，则可以解决重要的技术问题：能量沿着导线传递没有损失. 当然物理学的工作就是要解决这个问题.
只有根据量子力学，才能解释超导电性. 在$1957$年才给出了解释.
